pr_title: Add delay in emulated_hue after PUT
pr_body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->

## Proposed change

An Echo device changes the state of the device by submitting a PUT to `/api/{username}/lights/{entity_id}/state`. Immediately after the call, it executes a GET to `/api/{username}/lights/{entity_id}` to validate if the change was successful. 

In many cases the state of the device will not be updated to be reflected in the subsequent GET command. When there is a discrepancy between the state submited and received, Echo would complain with  '/.../ appears to be malfunctioning' announcement. This change introduces a short artificial delay of 250ms before the PUT method returns to allow for the change to successfully propagate, which keeps the Echo device pleased.

> I saw this is your first pull request. Welcome to the community!
> 
> Did you format your code with black? The tests are failing and pointing to that. It should happen automatically when you commit, maybe you committed using the `-n` flag to skip tests?

No, I am properly setting up the environment right now.
I tested these changes in my setup and it didn't seem to change much... The "device seems to be malfunctioning" error is still reported. Did it stop happening to you?

I was consistently getting this message before. After introducing 100ms delay it was significantly reduced, but one wall switch would still trigger the issue in approximately 50% of cases. Increasing it to 250ms seems to completely fix the problem.

I think the ultimate goal should be to check if the update already had effect on the changed object and return from the API when it does or after a predefined timeout. I am not in a position to implement that though, my Python is still a bit rusty...

There are multiple ongoing discussions here about this issue, and I hope this one could help fix it.

Since I don't have writing access to this repo, my approval of these changes is merely symbolic. You'll need approval from a maintainer for merging.

review_comments: What changes do we want to give time to propagate? Is it the service calls? If we want to wait for those why are we not awaiting them?

I think the service call might resolve almost instantaneously: exp. MQTT message being pushed to the broker. The service involvement finishes at this stage. This does not mean that the receiver of said message received it, processed and acted on it.

Ideally what would need to happen here is:
- invoke the service call - exp. 'turn-on light'
- check periodically if the service call had desired effect - exp. the light was turned on
- return only if the desired effect was observed or predefined timeout happened
 
Introducing the artificial delay is a easy to make hack/workaround - it works well enough without much of the code change...
